statements.claim: 284 carbon projects registered in Southeast Asia, 171.5 MtCO2e cumulative issuance as of 2023.
Nature-based-solution projects were 5.3% of projects but generated 73% of issuances, and ACMF flags NBS as carrying relatively high reversal and permanence risk in ASEAN.
From January 2007 to January 2025, only 1.73 MtCO2 of the 65.76 MtCO2 retired through ASEAN carbon-market projects was for ASEAN entities — 2.6%.

article6.explanation_en: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement lets a country sell an emission reduction it has counted. To stop the same tonne being claimed twice, the selling country applies a corresponding adjustment: it adds the transferred amount back into its own inventory, and the buying country subtracts it. The credit does not erase the emission; it moves who is allowed to count it.

statements: Carbon credits from projects hosted in countries without a Singapore Implementation Agreement are not allowed to offset carbon-tax liability under Singapore's ICC Framework.
Carbon tax-liable companies may use eligible International Carbon Credits to offset up to 5% of their carbon tax liabilities annually.

regional_framework.name: ASEAN Common Carbon Framework
regional_framework.status: Framework of five industry associations signed at COP29 (November 2024); operational work continuing through 2026. Not an ASEAN treaty.
regional_framework.explicit_non_goal: Uniformity. The stated objective is interoperability — the ability for different national systems to connect — not a single regional standard.

national_developments.item: Climate Change Act expected around Q3 2027; ETS and carbon tax expected to begin 2029–2030; voluntary credits may offset up to 15% of surrender obligations under the draft.
National Carbon Market Policy launched April 2026; carbon tax then ETS planned; alignment of Sabah and Sarawak carbon statutes with federal policy; Climate Change Bill expected in Parliament 2026.
Dual registry — SRN for compliance, SRUK for voluntary; IDXCarbon trading platform since 2023, open to global investors from 2025.
Piloting an emissions trading system with mandatory compliance targeted for 2028.
Foundational market infrastructure still being built.
Foundational market infrastructure still being built; Article 6 IA with Singapore signed.
Regional demand anchor; 12 Implementation Agreements; ICC framework with a 5% annual offset cap.

limitations: Issuance figures are cumulative registry statistics, not prices, not current-year flow, and not a quality-adjusted figure.
Brunei Darussalam is absent from the cited database and is not zero.
The two published regional totals (217.46 million and >350 million) come from different databases; neither is a ceiling.
Implementation Agreement status is time-sensitive and is re-checked manually, not by a feed.
Nothing here authorises, issues, retires or prices a credit. This is published context for screening.
